title: SCH-CNT-002 mech relic definition
description: A mech relic definition. The project-owned typed validator in src/MechaMiner.Content/Categories/ remains authoritative; this schema is the draft 2020-12 mirror kept for editor and tool interoperability, and a fixture corpus proves the two reach the same accept/reject verdict on every structural case. See content/schemas/README.md. The catalog-wide acquisition, rarity, stacking and registration blocks are not declared here: thirty-three of their keys were identical across all ten relics, and only the five that vary remain.

id.title: A stable, case-sensitive ASCII content ID

transformation_key.description: The localization key of the one-phrase transformation summary.

tradeoff_key.description: The localization key of the explicit tradeoff. Doc 40 requires the tradeoff to be explicit, so the field is required; the sentence itself is player-facing text, so the field holds a key rather than the words.

affected_scope.description: What the transformation applies to. At least one: a transformation that applies to nothing is not one, and doc 40 requires compatibility results computed against a scope.

minItems.derivation: the section requires compatibility results for all weapons, which is a computation over the relic's scope; a relic with an empty scope has nothing to compute against, so the floor is one and there is no ceiling below the vocabulary's own size

behavior_kind.description: The registered behavior, as a lower-kebab-case token. Whether it resolves to exactly one registered behavior descriptor is the behavior registry's check and is deliberately not asserted here. This token is NOT a mapping of the corpus's behavior_registration.hook prose, and the description that stood here said it was: it read the ten hook sentences as each naming one distinct hook point with none overlapping. Measured against the corpus that is false. There are nineteen hook points across the ten strings. Nine of the ten join two noun phrases with different head nouns by 'and', and both conjuncts are independently realised in the same file's effects block - REL-01's 'activation-rate transformation and opposite geometry' carries primary_activation_frequency_multiplier 3 for the first conjunct and mirrors_directional_and_targeted_geometry true for the second. Only REL-04, 'cadence/damage/area/duration transformation', names a single hook point. Three of the strings overlap each other on rate/cadence transformation: REL-01, REL-04 and REL-09. A relic-to-hook mapping is therefore not derivable today - it would need nineteen invented names and a document that mints them, which does not exist - so hook stays unmapped prose, no field here carries it, and this token asserts neither a hook vocabulary nor a one-hook-per-relic shape.

trigger_condition.description: What causes the relic's effect to fire.

effects.title: A registry-owned parameter map
effects.description: The relic's parameters, keyed by its behavior kind. The strongest case in the tree for an open map: seventy-four keys across ten relics with none shared between any two, so there is literally no common structure to factor. The key vocabulary belongs to the registered behavior descriptor rather than to this schema, so keys are not enumerated here; the strict codec still rejects a null, a duplicate key, and a non-snake_case key inside one.

pool_availability.description: Which pool this relic is drawn from.

unlock_id.description: The unlock that adds it to the cache pool. Present exactly when the pool token says the relic is behind one; the anti-correlated boolean that used to state the same fact a second time is gone.

sale_value_common_ore.description: What selling a displaced copy yields.

minimum.derivation: the section makes counts integral; this one is summed into a report column across the catalog, so zero is authored rather than omitted and the floor is zero rather than one

live_state_meter.title: A relic's live-state meter
live_state_meter.description: Present where the relic has live state.

rules.description: The accepted rule sentences for this relic.

cross_document_rules.description: Rules whose sentence travels with typed parameters. The one rule array in the tree that stays object-shaped, because unwrapping it would lose the numbers.

parameters.title: A registry-owned parameter map
parameters.description: The rule's typed parameters. The key vocabulary belongs to the registered behavior descriptor rather than to this schema, so keys are not enumerated here; the strict codec still rejects a null, a duplicate key, and a non-snake_case key inside one.

version.title: A positive integer version
version.description: The initial schema_version and content_version of every first-authored definition is 1.

minimum.derivation: the initial value of every first-authored definition is 1 and both versions only ever increment, so no valid version is below 1; there is no upper bound because a definition may be revised without limit

name_key.title: Localization key for the player-facing name

summary_key.title: Localization key for the concise player-facing summary

tags.title: Closed query and tooling vocabulary
tags.description: The vocabulary starts empty, so [] is the only accepted value.

presentation_id.title: Logical presentation entry, required absent
presentation_id.description: Required absent: a definition carrying this field is an error. No accepted document says what a presentation definition contains, so no ID grammar has been minted for one, and minting a shape for a category with zero members would be inventing structure ahead of need. The field was declared-optional with a non-empty-string constraint, which accepted any string an author invented and validated nothing about it; rejecting the field outright fails loudly the first time somebody adds one instead of accepting an unauthorized value. The subschema is 'not' over the empty schema, which rejects every instance, so the fault is the field's presence rather than its shape and an authored empty string is rejected by the same rule rather than as an empty declared-optional field. The typed validator reports MMC-2010 and names the field. When an accepted document mints a presentation ID grammar, this declaration becomes that grammar; until then it has no minLength, because a length bound on a value that can never be authored explains nothing.

allOf.title: an unlock reference follows the pool token
allOf.description: The anti-correlated boolean that used to state the same fact a second time is gone, so the token is the only thing that decides this.
